steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in onion and sauté until soft and translucent.

Stir in rice to coat grains with oil. Mix in cumin, chili powder, tomatoes, salt, and water. Cover, bring to a boil then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Tomato Rice
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican rice made with canned diced tomatoes, onion, chili powder, and cumin is easy to prepare for the flavor of Mexico in your kitchen!
raw_recipe.name: Mexican Tomato Rice

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in onion and sauté until soft and translucent.

Stir in rice to coat grains with oil. Mix in cumin, chili powder, tomatoes, salt, and water. Cover, bring to a boil then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally.

review.reviewBody: Wow, I thought this was best Mexican Rice ever. I used the Rotel tomato with green chilis and added some extra green chilis to spice it up. This is definitley a keeper!

This was awesome. I skipped the cumin since I didn't have any and used a whole can of Rotel that I had on hand. I added garlic powder a must for me. As recommended I used chicken broth in place of water (1 1/4 cup) and just a 1/2 tbsp of seasoning from a taco kit I was using. I did as it said and sauted the onions and then added the uncooked rice to coat w/ the oil but afterwards I added all of the ingredients into my rice cooker and let it do the work. It turned out delicious and my honey absolutely loved it better than the store bought mexican rice I usually make. I used salt to taste after rice was cooked.

Really good! I followed all of the directions as written except I used a little salsa instead of diced tomatoes (because it was already open) and after sauteing, before adding the broth (instead of water), I threw everything into my rice cooker and let it go. :) great recipe, easy to make.

It might be unfair for me to rate this as I changed it so much! But, I used 1 bag of instant rice instead of regular. I also do not like cumin or chili powder accept maybe in tacos as the taste is so strong! So, I just minced a clove of garlic. Lastly, I used vegetable broth in place of the water which adds a lot more flavor. Because I used instant rice it only needed to boil for about 5 minutes or less, an added bonus, as I was busy. This recipe is very adaptable, but if you like a milder rice skip the spices and add a clove of minced fresh garlic like I did. Was all eaten up with the chicken tacos it was served with!

This recipe seemed too simple to have this much flavor! This recipe rivals many restaurants. I substituted brown jasmati rice for white rice and chicken broth for water. I also left out the onion as my family isn't a fan of onions. We all thought it was delicious! It doesn't make a large quantity, so consider doubling if you're feeding 4 or more.

I made this tonight. I used chicken broth instead of water, I added a pinch of oregano (just because Mexican food usually adds oregano) a clove of garlic and Rotel Tomatoes w Chilies instead of just chopped canned tomatoes. It was amazing. There was nothing left. This will be our Mexican night side dish go to. I made it while our enchiladas were cooking. Its that quick and easy.

Tripled the cumin and chili pepper, almost a whole can of roasted diced tomatoes (semi drained) and the sauteed onion were all added for the last two minutes of the rice. Used a rice maker. Easy and excellent. Don't even like lots of spice, but "as is" is bland. Will add black beans next time to make this a main entree for a vegetarian meal.

This is a pretty sturdy and easy recipe. I typically use vegetable or chicken broth instead of water for a richer flavor. Sometimes I also add a can of green chili’s or use Rotel - whatever I have on hand. But overall, a crowd pleaser.

I followed the recipe but read suggestions to make adjustments. Instead of the tomatoes I used 1/3 can of Rotel tomatoes with Lime and cilantro. I also used chicken broth opposed to water. I would make this again!
Did not have canned tomatoes so used 1 Tbs tomato paste from a tube. Used chicken broth instead of water. Added 1 Tbs Southwest seasoning. Came out great.

This was really good, I used only organic ingredients and instead of canned tomatoes I used tomato paste. I also used a bit of curry powder instead of only cumin and vegetable broth instead of water. At the end I sprinkled a bit of lemon juice which gave it a nice tangy fresh flavor. I topped it with vegan homemade refried beans. Super Yum!
This was enjoyable but not excellent, only because I didn't have all the right spices and had to cheat with McCormick taco seasoning.
We really enjoyed this recipe. It was actually better that some of the Mexican rice served in some of our local restaurants. Best of all, it is super easy to fix.
Don't miss out on this dish! I added a few diced pickled jalapeños and garlic when I sautéed the onion and rice. Measurements and cook time was perfect for my liking.
yum

I made this recipe for dinner. I followed the recipe. It is good, other than my husband & I thought the chili powder was too strong. Reading the comments, next time I prepare this recipe I would use less chili powder & use Rotel instead of tomatoes.
Family loved it. Used chicken broth in place of water & reduced salt a bit
Very good rice with italian sausage ..yummmmy
I followed the ingredients as is and it tastes delicious! Easy to make.
Perfect! I substituted Rotel diced tomatoes with chillies.
